lesson.title: Mi Color Favorito: A Favorite-Color Survey
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol has a favorite color. Can you guess it? Sol is a sun, so Sol's favorite color is amarillo! Today Sol wants to find out YOUR favorite color.

Your [[favorito]] color is the one you love best. Pick up your favorite color — is it rosado? morado? azul? Hold that color card and say: 'Mi color favorito es el ___.' Sol says, 'Mi color favorito es el amarillo.'
Now be a color reporter! Ask everyone in your house, '¿Cuál es tu color favorito?' Each person picks a color and answers, 'Mi color favorito es el ___.' Try to remember every answer for tomorrow.
You told Sol your favorite color and asked your whole family theirs — 'Mi color favorito es el ___!' Tomorrow, we count up all the answers on a big color graph.

objectives: Say the sentence 'Mi color favorito es el ___' with their own favorite color in Spanish
Ask another person '¿Cuál es tu color favorito?' and listen for the color in the answer
materialsNeeded: Color cards, crayons, or objects your child can choose from — including the new colors
Paper to jot down each family member's answer for tomorrow's graph
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. With Sol, share that Sol the sun's favorite color is amarillo — 'Mi color favorito es el amarillo.'
2. Teach the word favorito ('favorite') and the sentence frame 'Mi color favorito es el ___.'
3. Have your child choose a favorite color card and say the whole sentence, filling in the blank — help with the color word as needed.
4. Practice the question '¿Cuál es tu color favorito?' ('What is your favorite color?') a few times together.
5. Send your child around the house as a 'color reporter,' asking each family member the question; write down every answer for tomorrow.
6. Come back to Sol and have your child report one or two answers: 'Papá — azul. Abuela — rosado.'
7. Close by asking: 'What is Sol's favorite color? What is yours?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: your child can say just the color word instead of the full sentence, and point to the card while saying it
Ready for more: your child adds a reason in English — 'Mi color favorito es el verde, like the grass'
Keep the written list simple — one name and one color word per person is all tomorrow's graph needs
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken speaking-and-surveying activity — success looks like your child saying 'Mi color favorito es el ___' with a real color and asking at least one other person the question. Save the family's answers for the Day 4 graph.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Hits week 6's WA-WL-2015.1.1 Interpersonal Communication target head-on: the child both tells their own favorite color and asks someone else theirs, a genuine two-way exchange. Matches the scope-and-sequence's Day 3 design (a favorite-color survey with 'Mi color favorito es...'), and the tally the child collects feeds directly into Day 4's counting graph.
